settings.identityDescription: Shown in the header and browser tab to tell servers apart.
settings.label: Label
settings.labelInvalid: Use up to 40 letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, underscores, or periods.
settings.labelError: Could not save the server label.
settings.consolePortDescription: After a change the console moves to the new port and the old one stops.
settings.portStarted: The port change has started. Wait a few seconds, then open the new address.
settings.portInvalid: Enter an unused port from 1024 to 65535.
settings.portError: Could not change the port. The original address is still available.
settings.modulesDescription: Install, remove, start and stop feature modules.
settings.logsDescription: Read the console and module logs.
settings.securityDescription: IP access, client certificates, sign-in limits, activity and the admin password. Asks for the admin password first.

security.weakPassword: Use 12 to 128 characters, with no spaces at the start or end.
security.allowlistFull: The allowlist holds at most 64 addresses.
security.passwordChanged: Admin password changed. Sign in again with the new password.
security.passwordDescription: After the change every session ends, this one included.
security.revokeDescription: The device can no longer sign in with this certificate. This cannot be undone; issue a new one if needed.
security.deleteDescription: The record is removed from the list and cannot be restored. This certificate is already revoked, so deleting it does not affect sign-in.
security.issueDescription: Issue a certificate for one device; the name helps you recognise it (for example "Home PC").
security.clearBanDescription: Clears the failure counts and bans of every source; banned addresses can try again at once.
security.networkDescription: One address or a range, such as 203.0.113.5 or 198.51.100.0/24.
security.revokeOthersDescription: Every device except this one is signed out.
security.barkKeysDescription: One key per device with Bark; every alert goes to all keys. Only the first and last four characters are shown, to tell them apart.
security.barkKeyNewDescription: The last part of the push URL in the Bark app.
security.barkKeyDeleteDescription: That device no longer receives alerts. You can add it again later.

dashboard.notInstalled: Module not installed. Install it in Settings → Modules.
dashboard.busy: Another module task is still running. Try again shortly.
dashboard.noTraffic: No traffic in this period yet.

modules.description: Install or uninstall optional modules. Uninstalling backs up the configuration and nodes, which come back when you reinstall. Feature switches are on Home.

logs.description: Logs from the console and each module. Clearing only hides the history here; the system log keeps it.

speedtest.description: Measure latency and bandwidth to this server from your browser.

traffic.invalid: Check the values: caps and speed limits must be above 0, and a set reset time must be in the future.

iperf.description: Open a time-limited iperf3 server on demand, or test from this server to another iperf3 server.
iperf.portDescription: Can only be changed while the server window is closed.

portfwd.description: Forward a public port on this host to another machine.
portfwd.deleteDescription: The public port stops forwarding immediately, and this rule's traffic record is removed too.

visitors.description: Addresses that recently connected to this server: console requests plus other inbound and outbound connections.

terminal.description: A root terminal on this server. Leaving the page disconnects it.

verify.description: This page can change the whole server. Enter the admin password again to continue.

files.description: Keep files on this server for a while and share download links that need no sign-in.
files.name: Name

backup.description: Back up and restore this server's configuration, with scheduled and encrypted backups.
backup.pick: Choose a backup to restore from the backup list.

tasks.description: Run commands on the server on a schedule; the configuration backup is listed here too.

closed.description: {name} is switched off on Home. Turn its switch back on there to use this page.

tailscale.description: Join this server to your tailnet and manage routes, exit nodes and devices.
tailscale.relaySet: A peer relay port is set; entering a new port replaces it.

domains.description: Forward subdomains over HTTPS to local ports; certificates and Cloudflare DNS records are handled for you.
domains.removeWithDns: Forwarding stops, the certificate is removed, and the DNS records on Cloudflare are deleted too.
domains.removeKeepDnsDescription: Forwarding stops and the certificate is removed; the DNS records on Cloudflare are kept.

ipcert.description: Give the console a trusted certificate on this host's public IP, so browsers stop warning.

frps.description: The FRP server on this host: FRPC clients elsewhere connect here and expose their ports on this server.

frpc.description: FRP clients on this host: connect to other FRPS servers to forward local ports, or reach their STCP proxies.

proxy.description: Manage the Singbox proxy nodes on this server: protocol, port, credentials, allowed destinations and traffic.
proxy.invalidDestinations: Some destinations are not valid. Enter one per line as described.

example.description: Replace with the real feature after copying the template.
example.toastDescription: Notifications appear at the top center. Success messages close after 4 seconds, failures after 8 seconds. Hovering pauses them.
example.toastSavedDetail: Settings updated. They stay after a refresh.
example.toastFailedDetail: The network connection dropped. Try again.

console.access_ip_error: Could not save the IP list.
console.access_ip_invalid: Enter one private IPv4 or unique-local IPv6 address.
console.access_load_error: The saved IP list could not be read. Password sign-in still works; adding a valid IP replaces the damaged list.
console.access_password_invalid: Passwords must match and the new password must be 12–128 characters.
console.alerts_error: Could not save the login alert settings.
console.alerts_intro: Push logins from new addresses and failed-login bans to your phone through Bark. The key is the last part of the push URL in the Bark app.
console.alerts_invalid: The server must start with https:// or http://; the key may contain only letters, digits, - and _.
console.alerts_load_error: The login alert settings file is invalid; alerts are treated as not set up.
console.alerts_on_ban: Alert when a ban is triggered
console.alerts_on_new_ip: Alert on login from a new address
console.alerts_status_off: No push key; no alerts are sent.
console.alerts_test_failed: The test alert failed. Check the server address, the key and the host's network.
console.alerts_test_sent: Test alert sent; check your phone.
console.audit_intro: The latest 50 logins and security setting changes, kept on the server (up to 500).
console.backup_contents: A backup holds all configuration and state: console settings, certificates and keys, nodes, FRP, domain forwarding, the Tailscale login and the service unit files. It does not include program code or the files in Mini Drive. Backups contain keys, so keep downloaded files safe.
console.backup_delete_confirm: Delete this backup? This cannot be undone.
console.backup_enc_off_text: Backups are not encrypted right now, and they leave out the data key (so they restore only on this host). After you generate a key pair, backups are encrypted and carry the data key, so they restore on any host.
console.backup_enc_on_text: New backups are encrypted to your public key. This server holds only the public key and cannot open them itself; restoring asks for the private key you saved. Public key fingerprint {fp}.
console.backup_enc_own: Or use a public key you already have (Base64)
console.backup_enc_regenerate_confirm: A key is already set. After regenerating, new backups open only with the new private key; existing encrypted backups still need the old one. Continue?
console.backup_error_ack_needed: This backup has risks; tick the confirmation before restoring.
console.backup_error_invalid: The input or file is not valid.
console.backup_error_key_needed: This backup is encrypted; enter its private key.
console.backup_error_key_wrong: The private key is wrong, or the backup is damaged.
console.backup_error_past: That time has already passed; choose a time in the future.
console.backup_key_done: I have saved it, go back
console.backup_key_page_text: The private key is shown only here, once, and the server does not keep it. Copy it now and store it safely; without it the encrypted backups cannot be opened.
console.backup_msg_restore_started: Restoring and restarting services; reload the page in a moment.
console.backup_restore_ack: I understand the risks above and still want to restore
console.backup_restore_effect: Restoring overwrites the current configuration with the backup's and restarts the related services; the console disconnects briefly. The current state is backed up first, and the result is shown at the top of the Backup page.
console.backup_restore_needs_key: This backup is encrypted. Enter its private key to see what is inside. The key is used for this one step and is not stored.
console.backup_restore_other_key: This backup is sealed to a different backup key than the one set now, so the current private key may not open it; you need the private key that matches it.
console.backup_restore_this_key: This backup is sealed to the current backup key.
console.backup_restore_warn_host: This backup comes from another host ({host}). Restoring it overwrites this host with its configuration, including the data key, login method and certificates.
console.backup_restore_warn_newer: This backup comes from a newer version ({version}) than the one running; restoring it may be incompatible.
console.backup_result_failed: Not completed: {name} — {error}. The current configuration was not changed.
console.backup_result_ok: Restored {files} files from {name}. The state before is saved as a "Before restore" backup.
console.backup_schedule_help: Backs up on the schedule you choose (repeating, or only once) and, for repeating ones, keeps only the latest few scheduled backups; manual and pre-upgrade backups are not affected.
console.backup_upload_help: Upload a backup file you downloaded earlier. After it is checked it appears in the list, where you can restore it.
console.client_cert_autoselect: Stop picking the certificate every time
console.client_cert_autoselect_help: Download the file for this device's system and run it; from then on the browser picks this certificate for the console without asking.
console.client_cert_current_none: This connection did not present a certificate.
console.client_cert_current_none_hint: No certificate on this device yet? Each device uses its own: enter a device name below to generate one; the page that follows has one-click setup files. If you already imported one and still see this, the browser was most likely not fully restarted.
console.client_cert_error: The certificate operation failed; the certificate files may not be writable.
console.client_cert_intro: Log in with a certificate instead of, or together with, the password: generate a certificate for each device, import it into the system or browser, and the browser presents it when the console opens. Choose the login method below; with "Certificate only" or "Password + certificate", a device without a certificate cannot even open the login page.
console.client_cert_issued_text: Note the import password. It is shown only once and the server keeps no private key; after leaving this page you can only generate a new one.
console.client_cert_keep_current: While certificates are required, the certificate this connection uses cannot be revoked.
console.client_cert_manual: Manual import (Android, iOS, Firefox, or if the one-click setup fails)
console.client_cert_name_invalid: The device name must be 1 to 40 characters.
console.client_cert_need_current: Import a certificate and reopen the console with it (this page then shows the certificate in use) before turning this on, so you cannot lock yourself out.
console.client_cert_openssl_missing: The bundled openssl is missing, so certificates cannot be generated. Running the installer again restores it.
console.client_cert_os_android: Android: Settings > Security > Encryption & credentials > Install a certificate > VPN & app user certificate, then pick the file.
console.client_cert_os_firefox: Firefox does not use the system store by default: import it separately under Settings > Privacy & Security > Certificates > View Certificates > Your Certificates.
console.client_cert_os_ios: iOS / iPadOS: open it in Files, then install it under Settings > Profile Downloaded.
console.client_cert_os_macos: macOS: double-click the file and add it to the login keychain.
console.client_cert_os_windows: Windows: double-click the file, choose Current User as the store location and Personal as the store (or let the wizard choose).
console.client_cert_required_text: This console only accepts devices with an imported client certificate. Import one, then fully quit and reopen the browser. If the certificate is lost, follow the README to restore password login as root on the server.
console.client_cert_setup_linux: Run it in a terminal with bash
console.client_cert_setup_macos: Double-click, then install it in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Profiles
console.client_cert_step_download: Download the certificate file. Downloading alone is not enough: browsers do not read certificates from the Downloads folder.
console.client_cert_step_import: Import it into the system certificate store, entering the import password above:
console.client_cert_step_restart: Fully quit and reopen the browser. Closing the window is not enough: Chrome and Edge may keep running in the background. Open chrome://restart or edge://restart, or quit from the system tray.
console.client_cert_step_setup: Download the one-click setup file for this device's system and run it, entering the import password above when asked. It imports the certificate and makes Chrome and Edge pick it on their own from now on.
console.client_cert_step_verify: Reopen the console's security settings. Once the certificate in use is shown, turn on Require client certificate. If the browser asks for a certificate, pick this one.
console.client_cert_steps_title: Next, complete these three steps in order
console.client_cert_tls_unsupported: This host's TLS library cannot verify client certificates (self test failed), so certificates are disabled. Update the system openssl/libssl packages, then generate a certificate again.
console.console_access_error: Could not save the console access list.
console.console_access_intro: When on, only listed addresses can connect to the console; others are dropped before the TLS handshake and never see the login page. Loopback is always allowed. LAN devices, Clash subscriptions included, must be listed too.
console.console_access_invalid: Enter a single IP address or a CIDR network.
console.console_access_keep_current: Removing this would lock out the current connection. Turn the limit off or add another entry that covers it first.
console.console_access_load_error: The console access list file is invalid; the limit is treated as off.
console.console_access_need_current: Add the current address first, or turning this on would lock you out.
console.console_access_recovery: If you are locked out, run this as root on the server to turn the limit off; no restart needed:
console.console_access_too_wide: A network covering every address cannot be added.
console.data_enc_error_text: The encryption status cannot be read; check /etc/vps-server/data.key.
console.data_enc_off_text: This host has no data key yet, so data is stored in plain text. Running the installer again (an upgrade) creates /etc/vps-server/data.key and turns encryption on.
console.data_enc_on_text: The console's password, sessions, alert key, audit records, access lists, Mini Drive index and scheduled tasks are stored encrypted ({encrypted}/{total} files). The data key is /etc/vps-server/data.key; do not back it up beside the data. Node, FRP, domain forwarding and Tailscale configuration must be read by those programs as they are, so it is not covered here but by the encrypted backups.
console.domains_add_help_manual: No Cloudflare token yet: enter the full name and point it at this host yourself. With a token you can pick the main domain.
console.domains_add_help_zones: Add a subdomain under a main domain the Cloudflare token manages: nas becomes nas.<main domain>; {'@'} means the main domain itself. DNS records and certificates are handled automatically.
console.domains_added: Added. The certificate is requested automatically once the name points here, usually within a minute or two.
console.domains_alert_cert_body: The certificate for {host} expires {date} and has not been renewed; check ports 80/443 and DNS.
console.domains_alert_dns_body: Cloudflare records for {host} could not be updated; see the domain forwarding page.
console.domains_alert_ip_body: {old} → {new}; DNS records follow the new address.
console.domains_aliases: Other names (optional, one per line, same target)
console.domains_allow_ips: Only these addresses or networks may connect (optional, one per line; empty means anyone)
console.domains_auth_help: Browsers ask for this user name and password first. Leave the user name empty for none.
console.domains_auth_keep: Leave empty to keep the current one
console.domains_backend_tls: The backend speaks HTTPS (its certificate is not checked; fits self-signed NAS or router pages)
console.domains_cert_detail: {issuer}, valid until {date} ({days} days left), renewed automatically
console.domains_cert_pending_detail: Waiting: Caddy requests it once the name points here
console.domains_dns_api: Cloudflare returned an error; it will be retried.
console.domains_dns_auth: Cloudflare rejected the token. Check that it is valid and can edit DNS for this domain.
console.domains_dns_detail: {kinds} record points here, DNS only; last synced {time}
console.domains_dns_manual: No token; point it here by hand
console.domains_dns_no_address: This host has no public IP address to publish.
console.domains_dns_no_token: No Cloudflare token yet; add the DNS records by hand.
console.domains_dns_unreachable: Cloudflare could not be reached; it will be retried.
console.domains_dns_zone: The token cannot see a Cloudflare zone for this domain.
console.domains_error_allow_invalid: Invalid address or network (at most 32), e.g. 203.0.113.7 or 198.51.100.0/24.
console.domains_error_auth_invalid: The user name may use letters, digits and . _ -; a new password needs 8 to 128 characters.
console.domains_error_caddy_rejected: Caddy rejected the new configuration; the previous one was restored. See the detailed logs.
console.domains_error_failed: The change failed. See the detailed logs.
console.domains_error_host_invalid: Invalid domain name. Enter a full name such as nas.example.com.
console.domains_error_no_public_ip: This host has no public IPv4 address to certify.
console.domains_error_port_invalid: The port must be 1 to 65535 and not 80 or 443.
console.domains_error_token_exists: This token has already been added.
console.domains_error_token_missing: That token no longer exists; it may have been removed.
console.domains_error_token_rejected: Cloudflare rejected this token. Check that it is correct and has Zone > DNS > Edit.
console.domains_error_zone_unknown: The token cannot see this main domain; reload the page and try again.
console.domains_ip_disabled: IP certificate turned off; the console is back on its self-signed certificate.
console.domains_ip_enabled: Enabled. The certificate usually arrives within a minute; the console picks it up on its own.
console.domains_ip_help: The console's existing https://<this host's IP>:<port> switches to a Let's Encrypt certificate, so browsers stop warning. The certificate lasts about 6 days and Caddy renews it; the port and the client-certificate requirement stay the same, and 80/443 do not serve the console.
console.domains_ip_off_confirm: Stop using the IP certificate? The console goes back to its self-signed certificate and browsers will warn again.
console.domains_more_options: More options: other names, allowed addresses, password
console.domains_site_disabled: Disabled. Requests to the name are dropped; DNS records and the certificate are kept.
console.domains_target_console: This console (Caddy checks the client certificate)
console.domains_token_clear_confirm: Remove the token “{name}”? DNS records of its domains stop updating automatically; existing records stay as they are.
console.domains_token_cleared: Cloudflare token removed. Existing DNS records are left as they are.
console.domains_token_help: Create an API token in Cloudflare with Zone > DNS > Edit for your domains. You can add several tokens (for example, domains in different Cloudflare accounts); each site uses the token that manages its main domain. Records are DNS only, and this host's IP is checked every 5 minutes.
console.domains_token_name_placeholder: Optional, such as the account name
console.domains_token_saved: Cloudflare token added and DNS records synced.
console.domains_upstream_host: Send the backend its own address as Host (for backends that only accept IP:port)
console.domains_zones_none: This token sees no main domains. Check its zone resources in Cloudflare.
console.files_delete_confirm: Delete "{name}" and all its download links?
console.files_error_busy: Three downloads are already running. Wait for them to finish.
console.files_error_incomplete: The transfer stopped early; the partial file was discarded.
console.files_error_no_room: Not enough room: over the limit, or less than 500 MiB would stay free on disk.
console.files_error_not_found: Not found; it may have been deleted.
console.files_error_quota_invalid: The limit must be between 0.1 and 10240 GiB.
console.files_error_rate_invalid: Enter a limit from 0.1 to 10240, or leave it empty for no limit.
console.files_error_too_many: Too many files. Delete some first.
console.files_error_too_many_links: This file has too many links. Revoke some first.
console.files_error_traffic_blocked: Mini Drive reached its traffic cap or validity period; uploads and downloads are paused.
console.files_error_url_blocked: This address points at this machine or a link-local address and is not allowed.
console.files_error_url_invalid: Enter an http or https URL.
console.files_fetch_help: This server downloads it directly, for sources other hosts cannot reach (GitHub Releases, for example). You can close the browser; the download continues in the background.
console.files_link_help: Anyone with a download link can download without a password or certificate; share it only with those who need it.
console.files_quota_help: Whatever the limit, at least 500 MiB stays free on disk. Lowering it deletes nothing; new files just wait until there is room.
console.files_rate_help: All download links together stay under this speed; downloads running at the same time share it. Leave empty for no limit.
console.files_upload_help: Choose a file and upload it; up to {room}.
console.frp_address_note: Use an address reachable from each FRPC instance. Add proxy entries in that instance’s configuration.
console.frp_client_binary_missing: FRPC is not installed on this host.
console.frp_client_note: FRPC instances on this host can be configured below. Existing connections stay active until you edit them.
console.frp_delete_client_confirm: Delete FRPC instance {name}? Its configuration will be saved for recovery.
console.frp_port_keep: Leave blank to keep the current port
console.frp_save_failed: FRP update failed. Existing settings were restored when possible.
console.frp_saving: Saving settings. If the connection drops, the result will appear when it reconnects.
console.frp_secret_keep: Blank: generated for a new proxy, current key kept when editing
console.frp_server_edit_note: The port or token change restarts FRPS. Update clients that use the old values.
console.frp_token_keep: Leave the token blank to keep the current value.
console.frp_unsupported_config: This FRPC configuration has settings the field editor cannot represent.
console.frp_visitor_note: A visitor listens on 127.0.0.1 on this host and reaches an STCP proxy on another FRPC using the same FRPS token and STCP secret key. The port is never exposed externally.
console.ipcert_failed: The change failed: there may be no public IPv4. See Settings > Detailed logs.
console.ipcert_ports: Port 80 must be reachable from the internet (Let's Encrypt validates through it). While on, Caddy holds 80/443 and serves the public reachability page, using this certificate for https://<this IP>/ too. No domain or Cloudflare token is needed.
console.iperf_client_busy: Another outbound test is already running.
console.iperf_client_failed: The test failed. Check the target server and its firewall.
console.iperf_client_invalid: Check the server IP, port, duration, rate, protocol, and direction.
console.iperf_client_missing: iperf3 is not installed on this host.
console.iperf_client_timeout: The target did not finish the test in time.
console.iperf_disabled: The iperf3 window is switched off in this install (VPSSRV_IPERF_ENABLE=0).
console.iperf_info: The window always closes itself — there is no "leave it running" option, because an open iperf3 server lets anyone saturate this host's uplink. Latency is the mean_rtt field of the JSON output.
console.iperf_missing: iperf3 is not installed on this host. Install it with: apt install iperf3
console.iperf_port_busy: Port {port} is already in use, so iperf3 could not start.
console.iperf_port_invalid: Port unavailable or the window is running.
console.login_ban_cleared: Failed login records and bans cleared.
console.login_ban_disabled: Failed login ban turned off. Failures are still recorded.
console.login_ban_empty: No failed logins since the web console started.
console.login_ban_error: Could not save the failed login ban setting.
console.login_ban_load_error: The failed login ban settings file is invalid; the ban is treated as on.
console.login_ban_observe_hint: When off, failures are still counted and a threshold hit is flagged instead of banned, so you can test detection. Switching clears current bans and flags.
console.login_ban_rule: After {count} wrong passwords from one IP (IPv6 grouped by /64) within {window}s, it is banned: {first} the first time, ten times longer for each repeat within a day, at most {max}. A successful login clears its count.
console.login_ban_switch: Ban IPs with too many failures
console.login_global_flagged: Global threshold reached, not paused ({seconds}s left).
console.login_global_rule: When all sources together get {count} wrong passwords within {window}s, password login pauses for {duration} for addresses that never logged in successfully.
console.login_mode_both_help: The device must present a valid certificate and the password must be entered; one alone is not enough.
console.login_mode_cert_help: Only a client certificate logs in; a device without one reaches nothing. The terminal and security settings still ask for the password.
console.login_mode_either_help: Either the password or a certificate logs in.
console.login_mode_hint: Before switching to "Certificate only" or "Password + certificate", open this page with an active certificate (the one in use is shown above), or you lock yourself out. If you lose the certificate, run `python3 /root/apps/vps-server/src/web/client_cert.py disable` on the server to go back to password only.
console.login_mode_password_help: Only the password logs in; a certificate the browser sends is ignored.
console.logs_clear_confirm: Clear the currently displayed history? System logs will be retained.
console.logs_clear_done: Historical logs shown here have been cleared.
console.module_public_needs_ipcert: HTTPS needs the IP certificate on
console.module_source_missing: Installer files are unavailable. Upgrade from a complete checkout first.
console.module_tailscale_asset_missing: The bundled Tailscale archive is missing. Rerun deploy/install.sh from complete source or an offline Release bundle containing the third_party/tailscale archive, extracted into a separate directory, while preserving the existing installation and state directories, then retry.
console.module_uninstall_confirm: Uninstall {name}? Its configuration and nodes are kept and backed up on the server, and restored when you install it again.
console.node_delete_confirm: Delete this node and revoke its share link?
console.node_keep_port: Leave blank to keep current port
console.node_meter_suspect: Incomplete metering; usage may be undercounted
console.node_overview_intro: Manage connection details and node settings in one place.
console.node_random_confirm: Confirm random port and credential reset; SNI stays unchanged.
console.node_route_hint: Format: IP, IP:port, network (10.0.0.0/24), domain, *.domain; a port is 443 or 8000-8100; IPv6 with a port is [fd00::1]:443. “Public Internet only” refuses private, loopback, link-local and 100.64.0.0/10 addresses; “Only the destinations below” refuses everything else. Domains are judged by the addresses they resolve to.
console.node_settings_failed: Node settings could not be applied.
console.node_state_unavailable: Node state is unavailable. Run the installer again to migrate or repair this installation, then reload this page.
console.portfwd_apply_failed: Forward could not be applied. Check the host firewall.
console.portfwd_howto: Uses this host's own iptables (DNAT + MASQUERADE); traffic passes through here on the way to the target, so the target sees this host as the client, not the original visitor. net.ipv4.ip_forward is turned on automatically the first time a forward is enabled, and is left on afterwards even if every forward is later removed — turning it back off is not automatic, since other software on this host may depend on it too.
console.portfwd_invalid: Check the port numbers (1–65535) and the target IP — one of them was not valid.
console.portfwd_module_disabled: Port forwarding is switched off in this install (VPSSRV_PORTFWD_ENABLE=0).
console.portfwd_port_taken: That public port is already used by this host or by another forward.
console.sessions_intro: A login lasts at most {ttl} and ends after {idle} without activity.
console.sessions_revoked: The selected devices were signed out.
console.sessions_use_logout: Use Log out for this device.

console.tailscale_exit_lan: Allow local LAN with exit node
console.tailscale_logout_confirm: Confirm logout; the current Tailscale connection may drop and reauthentication will be required.
console.tailscale_web_open_failed: Could not open the Tailscale web interface
console.task_delete_confirm: Delete the task {name} and its run history? This cannot be undone.
console.task_error_invalid: The task settings are not valid.
console.task_error_limit: The task limit has been reached.
console.task_error_past: That time has already passed; choose a time in the future.
console.task_month_day_help: 1 to 31; in a month without that day, its last day.
console.task_msg_started: Started; reload in a moment to see the result.
console.task_run_as_root: The command runs as root on the server and is stopped after the timeout; a task is not started again while its previous run is still going. The latest 20 runs are kept for each task.
console.task_schedule_help: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday, for example */15 * * * * is every 15 minutes; {'@'}daily and {'@'}hourly also work.
console.total_actual_gib: Usage the provider shows for this period (GiB)
console.total_calibrate_hint: The count can differ from what the provider bills. Enter the usage shown in the provider's panel for this period; the console stores the difference as a "calibration", shows it as its own bar above and includes it in the total; it clears itself when the next period begins. Leave it empty and save to clear the calibration.
console.total_hint: Adds up nodes, FRPS, domain forwarding, port forwarding, FRPC, Tailscale, iperf3, Mini Drive and speed test, counted as on their own pages (forwarded traffic ×2). Reset times are the server's local time; console pages, the terminal and SSH are not counted.
console.total_multiplier_note: Each figure is billed usage: nodes, FRPS and forwarding count every byte twice (in and out), so it is double what that feature's own page shows. The period runs from the reset day and includes what each source has already used in its current cycle.
console.total_over: The total traffic limit is reached. This only warns for now; nothing is throttled or cut off.
console.total_warn: More than 80% of the total traffic limit is used.
console.traffic_frpc_shared: These instances connect to the same server, so their traffic is counted and limited together: {names}
console.traffic_help_once: Upload is traffic coming into this host, download is traffic leaving it; each byte counts once. At the traffic cap it is slowed to 1 Mbps or cut off, as set.
console.traffic_help_tailscale: Counts traffic on the tailscale0 interface; traffic this host forwards (exit node, subnet routes) enters and leaves it, so it counts twice. At the traffic cap it is slowed to 1 Mbps or cut off, as set.
console.traffic_help_twice: Proxied and forwarded traffic enters and leaves this host, so each byte counts twice. At the traffic cap it is slowed to 1 Mbps or cut off, as set.

console.visitors_clear_done: History cleared. New visits and active connections will be recorded again.
console.visitors_clear_failed: Could not clear history. Try again.
